projectDescription: GitLab Attack Lab - A containerized GitLab pentesting lab for learning and practicing CI/CD security vulnerabilities
projectGoals: Provide a security research and pentesting lab for GitLab CI/CD
Enable learning of CI/CD pipeline security vulnerabilities
Automate setup and configuration of GitLab instances

architecture.description: Docker Compose-based lab with GitLab CE, runners, and pentester container

gitlab.description: GitLab CE instance running on Docker

runners.description: GitLab CI/CD runners for executing pipelines

pentester.description: Dedicated pentester container with security tools

scripts.description: Python automation scripts for setup and lab population
scripts.purpose: GitLab instance configuration, YAML merging, validation
keyFiles: populate-gitlab.py - Main GitLab populator using python-gitlab SDK
merge-scenarios.py - Merges base and scenario YAML configurations

lab-config.purpose: Define lab structure, users, groups, projects, and CI/CD templates

subdirectories.ci-templates: External CI/CD pipeline YAML templates for projects

keyFiles: base.yml - Base lab configuration (root user, pentester user)

tests.description: Test suite for lab setup and configuration validation
tests.purpose: Integration tests, static analysis, scenario validation
keyFiles: test_integration.py - Complete setup and component validation

test-data.description: Example CI/CD pipeline configurations for testing
test-data.purpose: Reference implementations of vulnerable and secure pipelines

keyFiles: CI_TEMPLATES.md - Guide for creating and using CI/CD templates

keyWorkflows.name: Complete Lab Setup
keyWorkflows.description: One-command setup: starts containers, initializes GitLab, creates users/projects, registers runners

keyWorkflows.name: Access Pentester Container
keyWorkflows.description: Enter pentester container for security testing and enumeration

keyWorkflows.name: Merge Scenario Configurations
keyWorkflows.description: Merge base configuration with scenario overrides into single YAML

keyWorkflows.name: Validate Scenarios
keyWorkflows.description: Validate scenario configurations for duplicates and reference integrity

keyWorkflows.name: Run Integration Tests
keyWorkflows.description: Validate complete lab setup, component availability, and configuration

CI/CD_Template_System.description: External file-based CI/CD template system to avoid YAML escaping issues
CI/CD_Template_System.reasoning: Complex bash scripts with special characters cause YAML parsing errors when embedded inline; external templates improve maintainability, reusability, and validation

Scenario_System.description: Modular scenario configurations that extend base lab configuration
Scenario_System.mergeProcess: scripts/merge-scenarios.py merges base.yml with scenario overrides

Lab_Populator.description: Python automation using python-gitlab SDK to configure GitLab from YAML

Docker_Compose_Infrastructure.description: Multi-container setup with GitLab, runners, and auxiliary services

setup: Ensure Docker and Docker Compose are installed
Copy .env.example to .env and customize if needed
Run 'make setup' for complete one-command initialization
Access GitLab at http://127.0.0.1 with credentials in README.md
configuration_changes: Modify YAML files in lab-config/ directory
Create new CI/CD templates in lab-config/ci-templates/
Run 'make merge-scenarios' to validate and merge configurations
testing: Run pytest tests/test_integration.py for complete setup validation
Run pytest tests/test_static.py for code analysis
Run pytest tests/test_ci_templates.py for template validation
Use conftest.py fixtures for common test setup
pipeline_testing: Create projects in GitLab with ci-templates/
pentesting: Use 'make pentester-shell' to access pentesting environment
Use GitLab API directly with personal access tokens

steps: Add groups, projects, users to scenario file
Include sensitive data exposure (API keys, tokens, credentials)
Reference in project definition in scenarios/
Run 'make logs' to view GitLab container logs
Use 'make shell' to access GitLab container directly
Check configuration with 'docker-compose exec gitlab-attack-lab gitlab-rails console'
Review .env file for token and password settings
Run 'make pentester-shell' to access pentester container
Configure pipeleek with admin token from .env

copilotHints.when_modifying_yaml: Remember that CI/CD templates use external files to avoid YAML escaping issues. Don't embed complex pipelines inline.
copilotHints.when_adding_features: Follow the scenario pattern: extend base.yml with scenario-specific overrides
copilotHints.when_writing_tests: Use conftest.py fixtures and GitLabTestClient for API interactions
copilotHints.when_working_with_containers: Verify health checks before assuming services are ready. Check docker-compose logs for startup issues.
copilotHints.when_handling_tokens: Tokens are generated during setup.sh and stored in .env. Use GITLAB_ADMIN_TOKEN for API operations.
